advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an empty-project fail-closed check to assert_datacenter_scope_ready (or correct the runtime docstring to state DC is not guarded).
evidence: runtime.py:299-311 docstring: 'No provider applies an implicit create-time project default (AC2) ... stays empty and fails closed in :func:`assert_cloud_scope_ready` / :func:`assert_datacenter_scope_ready` before any transport is built.'
assert_datacenter_scope_ready only builds `missing` from ('url', ...) and ('JIRA_PAT', scope.auth_present) — runtime.py:391-402; no check on scope.project or scope.query_project
Cloud path adds the guard (runtime.py:356-367 checks both query_project and project) but DC's readiness function was left unchanged, creating an asymmetry the docstring denies
advisory.finding: assert_datacenter_scope_ready does not check scope.project / scope.query_project, so after AC2 removed the implicit project default (and _resolve_provider_scope now returns raw_project verbatim for Data Center), a DC backend with an unset project has an empty write/read scope with NO fail-closed guard — contradicting the new runtime docstring which asserts DC fails closed via this function.
advisory.suggested_fix: In assert_datacenter_scope_ready, append the same empty-scope guards used for Cloud: raise BackendEnvError when scope.query_project.strip() or scope.project.strip() is empty.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm eager transport resolution on every persisting pass (incl. outbound-only/empty) is intended, or gate _resolve_pass_transport on the presence of inbound work as the prior path did.
evidence: reconcile_helpers.py:642-650 _resolve_pass_transport calls loader() whenever ctx.applier has a callable _load_acli, gated only by ctx.persist for the failure branch
applier.py:434-435: `if client is None and inbound_typed:` then `client = _load_acli()` — the ambient path built the client ONLY for inbound mutations

bind_operation_runtime re-raises on failure when ctx.persist (reconcile_helpers.py:677-679), so a compose/build/_load_acli failure now aborts a persisting pass that previously would not have touched the client
advisory.finding: bind_operation_runtime resolves the pass transport via _resolve_pass_transport -> applier._load_acli() unconditionally on every write (persisting) pass, whereas the applier previously only invoked _load_acli() when inbound_typed mutations existed (applier.py:434). This eagerly constructs the Jira client/transport (and re-raises composition/build failures for persisting passes) even for outbound-only or zero-mutation passes that never needed it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update bridge_check_access (_lib_ops.py:378) so the exit-2 message distinguishes the new missing_project reason from missing_credentials.
evidence: access_check.py new branch: `if not creds["jira_project"]: return None, ({"verdict": "INVALID", ..."reason": "missing_project"}, ["PROBE_FAIL reason=missing_project"], 2)`
_lib_ops.py:378-380: `if returncode == 2:` -> `message = "bridge access check requires JIRA_URL, JIRA_USER, and JIRA_API_TOKEN"` — consumer message not updated for the new missing_project reason
run_access_check previously defaulted `jira_project = ... or "DIG"` and proceeded; an unset JIRA_PROJECT now returns exit 2 where it previously succeeded
advisory.finding: run_access_check added a new 'missing_project' exit-2 failure mode, but its public consumer bridge_check_access branches on returncode==2 with a message that names only JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/JIRA_API_TOKEN — a missing-project failure now surfaces a misleading 'requires credentials' error.
scenarios: Operator runs `bridge check-access` with valid creds but unset JIRA_PROJECT: probe now exits 2 and the lib op reports a credentials error, not the true missing-project cause

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the run_access_check unset-JIRA_PROJECT fail-closed change is a documented, intended contract change for the capability probe.
evidence: Old: `jira_project = os.environ.get("JIRA_PROJECT") or "DIG"` (proceeded to probe)
New _resolve_probe_scope: `if not creds["jira_project"]: return None, ({..."reason": "missing_project"}, ["PROBE_FAIL reason=missing_project"], 2)`
consumers: src/rebar/_engine/jira-capability-probe.py:34 `_result, lines, returncode = run_access_check(...)`; src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:377
advisory.finding: run_access_check narrows its accepted input: an unset JIRA_PROJECT that previously defaulted to 'DIG' and produced a live probe verdict now returns exit code 2 (INVALID/missing_project). This is an unversioned behavior change to the public capability-probe surface consumed by jira-capability-probe.py and bridge_check_access.
scenarios: A deployment that relied on the implicit DIG probe target now gets a fail-closed exit 2

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the legacy_default '' (None) seed value is the intended stored-format contract and no reader assumes a non-empty legacy_default.
evidence: project_ensures.py: `return load_config().jira.project or ""` (was `or _DEFAULT_PROJECT` == 'DIG')
seed writes `"legacy_default": project` (project_ensures.py:110)
projects_store.py:96 `return Mapping(legacy_default=legacy_default or None, projects=projects)` coerces '' -> None
projects_store.py:129 `return mapping.legacy_default or None` — absent-bridge_project tickets now resolve to None rather than 'DIG'
advisory.finding: The store's projects.json legacy_default now records '' (coerced to None by the deserializer) instead of 'DIG' when jira.project is unset, changing the resolved fallback project for tickets with an absent bridge_project field on the committed store format.
scenarios: A fresh store initialized with no jira.project configured seeds legacy_default='' (None); previously-DIG-defaulted tickets no longer resolve to a project

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update docs/config.md:325 and docs/adr/0083:187 to reflect that no implicit 'DIG' project default is applied (AC2).
evidence: docs/config.md:325: `project = ""  # env JIRA_PROJECT  (the reconciler substitutes "DIG" when empty on CREATE)`
runtime.py now: `return auth, raw_project, raw_project` (no DIG substitution); backend.py `resolve_jira_settings()` (project_default dropped)

advisory.finding: Public config documentation still states the reconciler substitutes 'DIG' when jira.project is empty on CREATE, contradicting the code after the DIG-default removal — a config-contract doc drift.
scenarios: Operator reads docs/config.md and expects DIG-on-empty behavior that no longer exists
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the config.md comment to note that an empty jira.project fails closed (no DIG substitution).

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an empty-project (write and query scope) fail-closed guard to assert_datacenter_scope_ready to match assert_cloud_scope_ready and the AC2 invariant.
evidence: runtime.py:304-305 docstring: 'stays empty and fails closed in assert_cloud_scope_ready / assert_datacenter_scope_ready before any transport is built.'
runtime.py:312-314 DC branch returns (dc_auth, raw_project, raw_project) with no default after AC2 removed _CLOUD_PROJECT_DEFAULT
runtime.py:391-398 assert_datacenter_scope_ready only checks ('url', ...) and ('JIRA_PAT', scope.auth_present) — no scope.project / scope.query_project emptiness check
Contrast: runtime.py:356-367 assert_cloud_scope_ready raises BackendEnvError for both empty read scope and empty write scope
blocking.finding: assert_datacenter_scope_ready does not fail closed on an empty project scope, unlike assert_cloud_scope_ready which gained explicit empty write-scope (line 362) and read-scope (line 356) guards. After AC2 removed the DIG default, _resolve_provider_scope returns the DC project verbatim (empty when unset), so a Data Center write/query pass can proceed with an empty target project — contradicting the documented invariant that an unset project fails closed in BOTH assert_cloud_scope_ready and assert_datacenter_scope_ready.
scenarios: A Data Center reconciler run with jira.project / JIRA_PROJECT unset builds a backend and issues a write/query against an empty project scope instead of failing closed
blocking.suggested_fix: In assert_datacenter_scope_ready, after the url/JIRA_PAT check, raise BackendEnvError when scope.project.strip() or scope.query_project.strip() is empty, paralleling the Cloud guard at runtime.py:356-367.
